page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.1-4 is a compute-oriented virtual machine configuration belonging to the Standard family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and utilizes an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor operating at a base clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The virtual instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core via multithreading (2 threads per core), backed by 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

This server instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage, meaning runtime environments rely entirely on external network-attached block volumes for persistent disk storage. Hardware acceleration is absent, with a GPU count of zero. For connectivity, the deployment includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the processing units are dedicated rather than shared, performance remains consistent without CPU credit throttling or contention from neighboring tenants.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides a lean hardware footprint that remains cost-efficient for compute-bound tasks where large memory pools are unnecessary. The primary trade-off is the constrained 4.0 GB memory capacity, which limits usage for large in-memory caches or heavy database operations. Consequently, the VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.1-4 is best matched to lightweight microservices, front-end web serving, continuous integration runners, batch processing utilities, and auxiliary operational services.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.1-4 is an entry-tier, compute-focused virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 architecture. Driven by an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor clocking at 3.9 GHz, it supplies 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core alongside 4.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance provisions no onboard local storage, necessitating reliance on remote block storage solutions, and contains no discrete GPU accelerators. Network connectivity includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address. With dedicated core allocations ensuring uninterrupted CPU execution, the instance presents an economical profile for applications with modest memory requirements. It is well matched to workloads such as lightweight application hosting, microservices, automated build workers, proxy routing, and low-footprint background compute jobs.
